scenarios.hypothesis: A neighboring synthetic tenant may receive another tenant's unique canary when the requesting identity is not preserved as the effective retrieval principal through candidate filtering and context construction.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A dedicated controlled index containing synthetic canaries records candidate IDs, filter decisions, citations, and final context without reading any real-user data or external production source.
scenarios.positive_control: The owning synthetic principal retrieves its own unique canary with matching source lineage and citation under the expected tenant and authorization snapshot.
scenarios.negative_control: A neighboring synthetic principal issues the same semantically adjacent query but must not receive the other tenant's canary in model-visible or user-visible context.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would require searching real-user indexes, crossing the dedicated synthetic tenant boundary, or querying any uncontrolled production data source.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, the non-owner path cannot reach the canary while the owning principal still retrieves the same synthetic source with correct lineage and citation.
scenarios.principal_binding: Record authenticated principal, tenant, session, source owner, source ACL generation, and the effective retrieval principal actually consumed by namespace and filter policy.
scenarios.source_lineage: Trace the canary from the owning synthetic source object through chunk, embedding, candidate, citation, context, and any memory representation used by the tested request.
scenarios.derived_state_trace: Record derived IDs, namespace, index generation, cache generation, policy-generation binding, and downstream consumer so the returned canary can be tied to one controlled source.
scenarios.retrieval_policy_trace: Capture namespace selection, cache lookup, candidate set, ACL/filter input and output, reranker result, context builder result, and source/citation identifiers for both principals.
scenarios.lifecycle_state: Keep authorization, lifecycle, index, cache, and memory generations fixed during this baseline isolation scenario so identity binding is the only causal variable under test.
scenarios.cache_memory_state: Use a fresh cache and cleared synthetic memory for both principals to exclude stale cache reuse or prior memory contamination as the explanation for any observed canary.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold the query, source object, index generation, and model configuration constant while switching only the synthetic requesting principal and effective retrieval identity.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude model prior knowledge, duplicate synthetic fixtures, query-semantic drift, stale cache content, old session memory, citation rendering bugs, and test-cleanup contamination.
scenarios.leakage_level: A wrong-tenant candidate blocked before context is at most R1; wrong-principal context or citation is R2, and model/user-visible canary disclosure with lineage is at most R3.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Do not promote beyond the highest directly observed R-level or beyond observed evidence until identity binding, source lineage, controls, and the causal principal switch are demonstrated.

scenarios.hypothesis: A revoked or deleted synthetic object may remain policy-reachable after its owner-approved bounded convergence window because derived index, cache, citation, summary, or memory state was not invalidated consistently.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled test index and synthetic canary are queried only before, during, and after the documented convergence window while generation identifiers and no-op retrieval traces are recorded.
scenarios.positive_control: Before revocation or deletion, the authorized synthetic owner can retrieve the canary and matching source lineage, proving that the fixture and retrieval path are functioning normally.
scenarios.negative_control: After the bounded convergence window expires, the same now-revoked or deleted source must not be policy-reachable through retrieval, cache, summary, citation, or memory surfaces.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if the experiment would alter real retention state, delete production data, query uncontrolled indexes, or continue beyond the dedicated synthetic lifecycle fixture.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: The repaired lifecycle invalidation path removes policy-reachable stale representations within the documented window while unrelated authorized synthetic sources remain retrievable.
scenarios.principal_binding: Keep the synthetic requesting principal and tenant constant across the lifecycle transition so any post-transition accessibility is not confused with an identity or tenant switch.
scenarios.source_lineage: Bind every pre- and post-transition chunk, embedding, cache entry, citation, summary, and memory record to the deleted or revoked synthetic source object and its authorization snapshot.
scenarios.derived_state_trace: Track authorization generation, revocation generation, lifecycle generation, index generation, cache generation, and memory generation before and after the transition.
scenarios.retrieval_policy_trace: Record candidate creation, current ACL/filter decision, cache-hit behavior, context construction, citation resolution, and whether stale derived state bypasses current authorization checks.
scenarios.lifecycle_state: Record transition timestamp, owner-approved bounded convergence window, intermediate propagation states, and the first post-window query so expected asynchronous lag is separated from persistent policy reachability.
scenarios.cache_memory_state: Compare stale and fresh cache generations plus existing and cleared synthetic memory to identify which derived store, if any, preserves the canary after source revocation or deletion.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Repeat after rotating to a fresh cache and fresh memory while keeping the source lifecycle state unchanged; stale-derived-state hypotheses should track the affected generation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude expected asynchronous propagation within the documented window, stale test cleanup, duplicate source objects, unresolved citation metadata, clock skew, and model prior knowledge.
scenarios.leakage_level: Pre-window stale state does not by itself establish R4; R4 requires policy-reachable canary evidence after the bounded convergence window, while R5 additionally requires causal defect isolation.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Cap the finding below validated R4 until post-window timing, current authorization state, source lineage, fresh-state controls, and the policy-reachable stale representation are all demonstrated.

scenarios.hypothesis: A correctly filtered primary index may still yield a neighboring principal's synthetic canary when a stale cache entry or compacted memory record omits principal, tenant, policy-generation, or lifecycle-generation binding.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Mock cache and controlled synthetic memory stores expose generation, owner, and source-lineage metadata while an inert retrieval harness records whether a canary reaches model-visible context.
scenarios.positive_control: The synthetic owner can retrieve the canary through the correctly scoped cache or memory path, showing that identity-aware reuse remains functional for the intended principal.
scenarios.negative_control: A neighboring synthetic principal using the same semantic query must not receive the owner's canary from cache, compacted memory, or summary-derived state after current policy is applied.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop before replacing mock cache or synthetic memory fixtures with real account state, production conversation memory, broad cache inspection, or uncontrolled user data.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, cache and memory reuse are keyed and authorized by the required identity and lifecycle fields, while the owner positive control continues to reuse its own valid derived state.
scenarios.principal_binding: Record both requesting and effective retrieval principals together with cache owner, memory owner, tenant, source owner, and current authorization generation for every reuse attempt.
scenarios.source_lineage: Trace cached result, compacted summary, or memory record back to the original synthetic source object and canary, including the source ACL and derivation generation that created it.
scenarios.derived_state_trace: Capture cache key components, cache generation, memory generation, compaction revision, policy-generation binding, TTL or expiry, and the downstream context consumer.
scenarios.retrieval_policy_trace: Compare the primary index path with cache-hit and memory-hit paths to determine whether current ACL/filter checks are evaluated or bypassed when stale derived state is reused.
scenarios.lifecycle_state: Keep the source object stable while changing only identity or policy generation first, then test an explicit revocation transition separately to avoid mixing cache-key and lifecycle hypotheses.
scenarios.cache_memory_state: Run stale-cache, fresh-cache, existing-memory, and cleared-memory variants so the canary's persistence can be localized to one derived store instead of attributed to retrieval generally.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Rotate only cache generation or clear only the synthetic memory record while preserving query, source, principal pair, index generation, and model configuration; the result should track the defective store.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude primary-index leakage, duplicate canaries, model memorization, test-session reuse, citation-only staleness, TTL timing, query differences, and malformed mock cache semantics.
scenarios.leakage_level: A stale internal cache candidate blocked before context remains R1; wrong-principal context may reach R2 or R3, while R5 requires a repeatable causal cache or memory binding defect with controls.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Do not report a general RAG isolation failure when the evidence localizes only to cache or memory coherence; cap the claim to the directly observed store, R-level, lifecycle state, and causal control.
